writeup: TIC 355737250 is a candidate eclipsing binary star with an orbital period of 9.168253 days, detected through automated analysis of TESS photometry. The primary eclipse produces a 4.72% dimming, while no secondary eclipse was detected. The signal reached a detection significance of 145.2 in the box-least-squares search, and pixel-level analysis confirmed the signal with a peak signal-to-noise ratio of 21.6, though the centroid offset of 4.3 arcsec warrants attention. The candidate does not appear in any of six checked variable-star catalogs. However, alternating eclipses show significantly different depths, suggesting the true orbital period may be double the initially measured value - a data quality pattern that indicates caution in interpreting this candidate as a straightforward eclipsing binary.
